questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Environment: Functions and Resource Depletion' refers to.
questions.a: Environment supplies resources, absorbs waste, sustains life and provides aesthetic services; resource depletion arises when extraction exceeds regeneration and waste generation exceeds absorption capacity, threatening the carrying capacity of the environment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Environment: Functions and Resource Depletion'.
questions.a: Sustainable development meets the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Environment: Functions and Resource Depletion' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Environment and sustainable development (source: keec107.txt environment functions sections)

concepts.title: Global Warming, Ozone Depletion and Pollution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Global Warming, Ozone Depletion and Pollution' refers to.
questions.a: Environmental degradation includes global warming from greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and methane, ozone depletion from chlorofluorocarbons thinning the protective ozone layer, and air, water, land and noise pollution from industrial and household wastes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Global Warming, Ozone Depletion and Pollution'.
questions.a: The Kyoto Protocol sets emission reduction targets for greenhouse gases, and control measures cover cleaner fuels, catalytic converters and treatment of effluents.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Global Warming, Ozone Depletion and Pollution' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Strategies for Sustainable Development in India

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Strategies for Sustainable Development in India' refers to.
questions.a: Sustainable development strategies include use of non-conventional energy like solar, wind and hydel power, cleaner LPG and gobar gas, compressed natural gas in transport, bio composting, biopesticides, traditional knowledge and prudent water and forest use.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Strategies for Sustainable Development in India'.
questions.a: Shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy and recycling resources keeps development within environmental limits.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Strategies for Sustainable Development in India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Strategies for sustainable development (source: keec107.txt strategies sections)
